papers.title: Prediction of First and Recurrent Falls in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and externally validate prediction models for next-year falls in Parkinson's disease (PD), and to evaluate the incremental value of imaging and fluid biomarkers. METHODS: We developed models in Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) to predict next-year falls with external validation in University of Pennsylvania (UPenn) cohorts. We evaluated incident falls among visits without current or prior falls and recurrent falls among visits with current falls. We calculated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and development-derived risk strata. RESULTS: The incident model, comprising Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale Part III, Montreal Cognitive Assessment, and Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS), was developed in 773 visit-pairs and validated in 589 visit-pairs. AUROC was 0.704 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.653-0.750) in PPMI and 0.630 (95% CI = 0.564-0.687) in UPenn. Incident fall risk increased from 7.1 to 18.5% across low- to high-risk groups in UPenn. The recurrent model, comprising Hoehn and Yahr (H&Y), GDS, and Symbol Digit Modalities Test, was developed in 302 visit-pairs and validated in 137 visit-pairs. AUROC was 0.683 (95% CI = 0.623-0.753) in PPMI and 0.641 (95% CI = 0.538-0.732) in UPenn. Recurrent fall rates increased from 22.2 to 65.0% across low- to high-risk groups in UPenn. Exploratory biomarker augmentation modestly improved discrimination beyond clinical models in PPMI, but not in external validation, where estimates were imprecise. INTERPRETATION: Clinical measures may identify next-year fall risk in PD with moderate discrimination, although performance attenuated in external validation. Exploratory biomarkers provided modest incremental value in development but not in external validation. ANN NEUROL 2026.

papers.title: When gait reveals emotion: recognition through gait videos in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Gait disturbances represent a hallmark of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet gait is increasingly recognized as not solely a motor function but as a dynamic channel for emotional expression. PD patients might exhibit deficits in recognizing emotions and emotional blunting, characterized by reduced valence and intensity ratings. However, whether individuals with PD can perceive emotional states from human gait remains unexplored. OBJECTIVES: This study examined whether PD individuals can recognize emotions from gait videos and whether they show selective impairments in emotional appraisal, with respect to healthy controls (HC) matched for age and sex. METHODS: Thirty-eight individuals with PD and 38 HC completed an online questionnaire including 12 videos of an actress walking with gait patterns expressing six emotions (i.e., happiness, sadness, fear, anxiety, anger, and neutral), each shown with blurred or visible facial expressions. Participants identified the expressed emotion and rated its valence and intensity. Accuracy in emotion recognition and valence and intensity scores were compared between and within groups and between conditions (i.e., blurred-face vs facial expression). RESULTS: Recognition accuracy and valence ratings were largely preserved in PD. PD participants reported lower overall emotional intensity than HC, without evidence of an emotion-specific reduction. CONCLUSIONS: PD patients display reduced emotional appraisal regarding intensity yet generally retain the ability to recognize emotions and their valence from gait. These findings may inform future research on the potential integration of emotional gait stimuli into action observation training programs.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction as a Convergent Mechanism of α-Synuclein Toxicity: A Systematic Review of In Vitro Fibrillar Models.
papers.abstract: Synucleinopathies, including Parkinson's disease, Dementia with Lewy bodies, and Multiple System Atrophy, are characterised by intracellular accumulation of misfolded α-synuclein (αSyn). Although αSyn aggregation is central to disease pathogenesis, the mechanisms linking αSyn to progressive neurodegeneration remain incompletely understood. Mitochondrial dysfunction is recognised as a key pathological process, particularly in experimental models using exogenously applied αSyn species, including preformed fibrils (PFFs). This systematic review synthesises evidence from mammalian in vitro studies that examined the effects of disease-associated αSyn conformations, including monomers, oligomers and PFFs, on mitochondrial structure and function. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, EMBASE, MEDLINE, and PsycInfo were searched to identify eligible peer-reviewed studies published up to March 2026, yielding 33 included studies. Models encompassed neuronal, astrocytic, microglial, endothelial, fibroblast, and induced pluripotent stem cell-derived systems, enabling comparison across cell types, αSyn conformations, and genetic backgrounds. Across included studies, oligomeric and fibrillar αSyn consistently induced mitochondrial depolarisation, impaired oxidative phosphorylation, reduced ATP production, complex-I dysfunction and increased reactive oxygen species generation. Additional mitochondrial pathological changes included fragmentation, cristae disruption, impaired TOM20-mediated protein import, calcium dysregulation, defective mitophagy and increased heteroplasmy i.e. accumulation of damaged mitochondria. These alterations frequently preceded cell death and were amplified in dopaminergic and genetically vulnerable models, including αSyn A53T, SNCA triplication, and PARK2-associated transgenic systems. Our review highlights mitochondrial dysfunction as a mechanism underlying αSyn toxicity, whilst suggesting methodolog

papers.title: Deep Eutectic Solvents Improve Protective Effects of Quercetin against Cytotoxic Amyloid Fibrillation of α-Synuclein.
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.abstract: Natural polyphenols are among the most frequently investigated small molecules showing promising therapeutic effects against neurodegenerative diseases. However, drawbacks such as poor aqueous solubility and bioavailability have significantly restricted the biological applications of polyphenols, leading to research to overcome these limitations. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) are a new class of green and biocompatible solvents with multiple applications, including their use to increase the aqueous solubility and bioavailability of natural polyphenols. This finding motivated us to investigate the effect of ethaline, a DES composed of choline chloride and ethylene glycol, on the capacity of quercetin in modulating the cytotoxic amyloid fibrillation of α-synuclein (α-syn). The results showed that dissolving quercetin in ethaline considerably increased the potential of quercetin to inhibit cytotoxic fibril formation of α-syn. We suggest that increasing the aqueous solubility of quercetin is likely the main mechanism contributing to the beneficial effects of ethaline. Thanks to its enhanced aqueous solubility, quercetin would interact more effectively with surrounding molecules, including α-syn monomers and reactive oxygen species. This increases not only the anti-amyloidogenic effects of quercetin, but can also improve its antioxidant activity, leading to more effective inhibition of α-syn fibrillation process as well as protecting cells against damage induced by α-syn aggregates. These findings may suggest that DESs could serve as new candidates to increase the therapeutic effects of polyphenols in relation to neurodegenerative diseases, including Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: Understanding Glymphatic's Role In Proteinopathies (GRIP): A single centre case-control study protocol.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) are proteinopathies characterized by pathological accumulation of amyloid beta, phosphorylated-tau, and alpha-synuclein. Impaired clearance of these proteins is thought to contribute to disease pathogenesis, whereas preserved or enhanced clearance may be compensatory. Beyond intracellular degradation within neurons and glial cells, an extracellular clearance pathway, the glymphatic system, facilitates cerebrospinal fluid flow into perivascular spaces, exchange with interstitial fluid, and subsequent clearance from the brain. Glymphatic transport may therefore be critical for removal of excess proteins and metabolic waste, and its dysfunction could promote protein aggregation and neurodegeneration. The Glymphatic's Role In Proteinopathies (GRIP) study is an observational case-control imaging and biomarker study comparing glymphatic clearance in patients with AD, PD, and DLB versus healthy controls. We aim to recruit 70 participants: PD (n = 20), DLB (n = 10), AD (n = 20), and age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n = 20). The AD group will be stratified by pathology, with half amyloid-positive/tau-negative (A + T-) and half amyloid- and tau-positive (A + T+). The PD group will be stratified by disease duration. Participants will undergo baseline MRI followed by intrathecal injection of gadobutrol (0.25 mmol) and serial MRI at 5, 24, 48, and 72 hours. Influx and efflux of tracer will be modeled from T1 signal changes. Blood will be sampled repeatedly from 1 to 72 hours; cerebrospinal fluid will be collected at baseline. Individual glymphatic clearance will be estimated using population pharmacokinetic methods, where gadobutrol serves as a tracer. Sleep will be monitored with triaxial accelerometry and sleep diaries. The primary outcome is group differences in glymphatic clearance metrics between ea

papers.title: Intranasal Mitochondria-Targeted Rosmarinic Acid Selenium Nanoparticles Restore Mitochondrial Function and Attenuate Dopaminergic Neurodegeneration in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and α-synuclein pathology, highlighting the need for mitochondria-targeted neuroprotective strategies. Here, we developed a mitochondria-targeted intranasal nanotherapeutic system comprising rosmarinic acid (RA)-loaded selenium nanoparticles (RASNPs) surface-functionalized with triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-conjugated chitosan (TCS-RASNPs) to enhance nose-to-brain delivery and improve mitochondrial function. TCS-RASNPs exhibited a spherical morphology, a uniform particle size distribution (140.13 ± 0.40 nm), a narrow polydispersity, and a positive surface charge (33.7 ± 0.75 mV), indicating good colloidal stability. Spectroscopic characterization confirmed successful RA loading and surface functionalization. Moreover, TCS-RASNPs enhanced antioxidant activity and sustained drug release compared with free RA and unmodified RASNPs. In neuronal cells, TCS-RASNPs significantly enhanced neuronal survival, reduced apoptosis, attenuated intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and improved mitochondrial membrane potential under 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium (MPP+)-induced neurotoxicity. Confocal microscopy further confirmed efficient mitochondrial localization of TCS-RASNPs. Pharmacokinetic and biodistribution studies demonstrated prolonged retention of RA and significantly higher brain RA levels following intranasal administration. In 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced Parkinsonian mice, TCS-RASNPs increased tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression, reduced α-synuclein (SNCA) expression, and normalized oxidative stress biomarkers in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and striatum (STR) regions. papers.title: Exploring Contributors to Fear-Based Activity Avoidance in Parkinson Disease: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Depression, Balance, and Disease Severity.
papers.journal: Journal of neurologic physical therapy : JNPT
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Fear of falling (FoF) avoidance behavior (FFAB) is common in Parkinson disease (PD) and contributes to reduced activity, deconditioning, and functional decline. Although depression, anxiety, fatigue, cognition, balance, and motor severity have been examined in relation to FoF, few studies have evaluated them simultaneously. The purpose of this exploratory study was to identify the relative contributions of affective, cognitive, fatigue-related, balance, and motor factors associated with FFAB in individuals with early-stage PD and to generate hypotheses for future investigation. METHODS: A cross-sectional secondary analysis was conducted in mild to moderate PD (Hoehn and Yahr stages 1-3, n = 35). Participants completed measures of FFAB (modified FFAB Questionnaire), fatigue (Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson Disease Rating Scale [MDS-UPDRS] Part I, item 13), mood (Parkinson Anxiety Scale and Geriatric Depression Scale), cognition (Mini-Mental State Exam, Trail Making Test Parts A and B, and Symbol Digit Modalities Test), balance (MiniBESTest [MBT]), and motor severity (MDS-UPDRS Part III). Bivariate correlations were computed between FFAB and candidate predictors, followed by Elastic Net regression. RESULTS: Modified FFAB Questionnaire scores were strongly correlated with depressive symptoms and balance. Elastic Net regression retained 11 variables, including Geriatric Depression Scale (β = 616), MBT (β = -0.469), MDS-UPDRS Part III (β = 0.156), sex (β = 0.183), Trail Making Test Part A (β = 0.115), and fatigue (β = 0.050). Bootstrap confidence intervals indicated that MBT demonstrated the most stable association with FFAB (95% confidence interval: -0.703, -0.169). DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: FFAB in early-stage PD appears strongly associated with depressive symptoms and balance impairment, with modest contributions from motor severity. papers.title: Scutellarin as a multi-target neuroprotective agent: analytical evidence, pharmacokinetic insights and translational strategies across neurodegenerative disorders.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are a leading cause of disability and mortality globally, but effective disease-modifying therapeutic strategies are still largely unavailable. Scutellarin is a flavonoid glycoside extracted from Erigeron breviscapus (Vant.) Hand-Mazz. It has been widely studied in preclinical models of neurodegenerative disorders. In this study, we performed a systematic review of preclinical animal studies. We combined comprehensive database retrieval with quantitative synthesis of eligible outcomes. The pooled results demonstrated that scutellarin significantly reduced cerebral infarct volume and improved neurological deficit scores in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion models. It also ameliorated learning and memory impairments in experimental Alzheimer's disease (AD) models. Consistent neuroprotective effects were also found in models of depression, anxiety, Parkinson's disease, etc. Mechanistic analysis indicated that scutellarin produces multi-level neuroprotective effects. It acts by reducing oxidative stress, inhibiting neuroinflammation, suppressing apoptosis, stabilizing the neurovascular unit and other neurobiological processes. This review first evaluated the preclinical efficacy of scutellarin through systematic review and meta-analysis. It then integrated cross-disease mechanisms with network pharmacology, reverse virtual screening and molecular docking to identify computationally predicted targets. Although scutellarin shows promising preclinical effects, its clinical translation faces major limitations. These limitations include low oral bioavailability, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and insufficient data on brain exposure. Overall, scutellarin is a multi-target neuroprotective candidate. Future studies should focus on target validation, exposure-response modeling, delivery optimization and clinically relevant translational evaluation.

papers.title: Inferior Frontal Gyrus Alterations in Freezing of Gait in Parkinson's Disease Without Evidence for Overall Hemispheric Lateralization: A Systematic Review and Activation Likelihood Estimation Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Freezing of gait (FOG) is one of the most debilitating motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD). Prior studies have suggested a potential right-hemispheric preference in the pathophysiology of FOG. Yet, there is limited evidence regarding which brain regions are most consistently associated with FOG and whether these alterations indeed show right-hemispheric lateralization. We aimed to identify brain regions associated with FOG based on multimodal neuroimaging findings and to examine their hemispheric lateralization. A systematic review across multiple neuroimaging modalities was performed, followed by an activation likelihood estimation (ALE) coordinate-based meta-analysis to assess convergent brain alterations in PD patients with FOG (freezers) versus those without FOG (nonfreezers). Hemispheric lateralization was assessed using the distribution of reported stereotactic coordinates. The systematic review included 108 articles, of which 33 were included in the primary ALE meta-analysis. We identified a significant convergent cluster in the right inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) pars opercularis/dorsolateral prefrontal cortex in PD freezers compared with nonfreezers. No evidence of overall hemispheric lateralization was observed based on the distribution of reported coordinates. Our findings identify the right IFG as a consistent neural correlate of FOG, potentially reflecting heightened frontal recruitment, with no clear evidence of hemispheric lateralization. The lack of further consistency in brain regions could reflect the known heterogeneity in the pathophysiology of FOG.

papers.title: Effects of pathway shape and dual-tasking on spatiotemporal gait parameters in individuals with Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Examining the effects of different pathway shapes on walking performance, particularly under cognitive load, is important for understanding motor control in individuals with Parkinson's disease (PD) under real-life conditions. This study aimed to investigate the effects of walking on different pathway shapes and dual-tasking (DT) on spatiotemporal gait parameters in individuals with PD. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A prospective cross-sectional observational study was conducted with 50 individuals diagnosed with PD. Participants were initially assessed using the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS), the Dual-Task Questionnaire (DTQ), and the Modified Gait Efficacy Scale (mGES). Subsequently, spatiotemporal characteristics of the 4-Meter Walk Test (4MWT), Timed Up and Go Test (TUG), Figure-of-8 Walk Test (F8WT), and L Test were measured under single-task and DT conditions. RESULTS: In all tests, dual-task conditions significantly increased duration and step count (p CONCLUSIONS: Dual-task conditions impair both straight and shaped walking in PD. While 4-MWT exhibits higher time-space costs, DTQ and UPDRS-III selectively determine dual-task performance across different pathway shapes. Integrating both straight and curved paths under cognitive load provides a more comprehensive approach for clinical assessment and rehabilitation.

papers.title: Association between self-reported physical activity levels and patient reported cognitive problems in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cognitive dysfunction is a highly impactful symptom experienced by some people with Parkinson's disease (PD). Physical activity may slow cognitive impairment in PD. OBJECTIVE: Evaluate associations between self-reported physical activity and prevalence and incidence of bothersome cognitive problems, as measured by the PD-Patient Report of Problems (PD-PROP). METHODS: 22,760 participants in Fox Insight (FI), an online, longitudinal study, completed Physical Activity Scale of the Elderly (PASE) and PD-PROP, a patient-reported outcome measure through which people with PD (PwP) report their 5 most bothersome problems related to PD. Associations between PASE and reports of cognitive problems (classified using a combination of human curation, natural language processing, and machine learning) were evaluated cross-sectionally. 9114 participants with follow-up PD-PROP assessments and no reported cognitive problems at baseline were included in longitudinal analyses to determine if physical activity levels at baseline are associated with incident reporting of cognitive problems. RESULTS: At baseline, 32% reported at least one cognitive problem and had lower PASE Leisure scores compared with participants who did not report cognitive problems. Lower levels of physical activity were associated with increased odds of reporting cognitive problems, particularly in categories of memory (OR = 0.913), language/word finding (OR = 0.923), and cognitive impairment not otherwise specified (OR = 0.880). Longitudinally, lower baseline self-reported physical activity levels were associated with incident reporting of cognitive problems, particularly memory impairment. CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported physical activity levels are modestly associated with both increased prevalence and incident bothersome cognitive problems on the PD-PROP. papers.title: Effects of STN-DBS on voluntary facial mimicry in Parkinson's patients: a pilot study.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Parkinson disease (PD) causes hypomimia, an early manifestation driven by motor, limbic and basal ganglia dysfunction that impairs nonverbal communication. Traditional clinical rating scales used to assess facial expressivity are subjective, traditional clinical scales are subjective, whereas automated video analysis based on the Facial Action Coding System (FACS) provides an objective, fine-grained measurement of specific facial Action Units (AUs). Subthalamic Deep Brain Stimulation (STN-DBS), a widely adopted therapy for PD, modulates basal ganglia circuits, yet its precise effect on facial mimicry remains poorly characterized. This study evaluates how STN-DBS influences voluntary facial expressivity by comparing Stim-ON/Med-ON and Stim-OFF/Med-ON states. METHODS: 18 PD-patients with STN-DBS were evaluated in two experimental conditions (Stim-ON/Med-ON VS Stim-OFF/Med-ON). Video recordings captured participants reproducing seven voluntary facial expressions (six basic emotions plus neutral). Facial mimicry was quantified using OpenFace 2.0 to extracts AUs intensities according to the FACS system. RESULTS: MDS-UPDRS-III scores improved significantly in the DBS-ON state (p < 0.001), confirming the expected improvement in motor symptoms. Automated FACS analysis revealed emotion-specific differences in AUs, showing reduced mimicry in the Stim-OFF/Med-ON condition, for neutral (AU06, p = 0.042), happiness (AU06, p = 0.034), fear (AU25, p = 0.043), and anger (AU23, p = 0.036). For sadness, AU09 activation was higher in the OFF state (p = 0.021). No significant differences emerged for disgust or surprise. CONCLUSION: STN-DBS appears to selectively modulate voluntary facial mimicry in PD, enhancing activation of emotion-relevant AUs, and reducing non-pertinent activations for sadness. These findings indicate that STN-DBS influences emotional motor output beyond classical motor con

papers.title: Comparison of Postural Control During Activities of Daily Living Between Trained Individuals With Parkinson's Disease and Healthy Older Adults With Different Exercise Levels.
papers.journal: Journal of aging and physical activity
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare postural control (PC) during activities of daily living between trained individuals with Parkinson's disease and healthy individuals who practiced physical exercise and those who did not. METHODS: This is a case-control study, in which 105 individuals were assigned to groups: 35 individuals with Parkinson's disease who underwent neurofunctional physiotherapy (GDP-T), 35 healthy individuals who practiced exercise (G-EX), and 35 healthy individuals who did not practice exercise (G-NEX). The Activities-specific Balance Confidence Scale was used to assess participants. PC was assessed by posturography in the following conditions: (a) bipedal position, (b) feeding task, (c) getting dressed task, and (d) executive function task. The parameters evaluated were center of pressure (COP) area (in square centimeters), amplitude (in centimeters), and anteroposterior and mediolateral speed (in centimeters per second). RESULTS: GDP-T showed less balance confidence than the other groups. There was no significant difference between the groups in the bipedal position. G-NEX showed a greater COP area, amplitude, and speed of movement (anteroposterior and mediolateral) compared with G-EX and GDP-T in the functional tasks. G-EX showed a smaller COP area in the getting dressed task and greater speed in executive function compared with GDP-T. CONCLUSION: The PC of GDP-T was similar to that of G-EX, although its balance confidence was lower. G-NEX showed greater variation in the COP parameters for the variables analyzed in all tasks. Significance/Implications: Regular exercise has been shown to overcome the clinical characteristics of Parkinson's disease and provide a positive PC response to specialized training in both typical and atypical aging.

papers.title: Levodopa and Subthalamic Nucleus Deep Brain Stimulation Modulate Excitation/Inhibition Balance and the Neural Encoding of Isochronous Sequences in Persons With Parkinson's Disease.
papers.journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract: Temporally regular auditory stimuli, as found in isochronous sound streams, metronome beats, or music, are often used in rhythmic auditory stimulation (RAS) interventions to initiate and stabilize the temporal coordination of motor plans in persons with Parkinson's disease (pwPD). Research suggests that RAS promotes the recruitment of a cerebellar-prefrontal network and recalibrates abnormal β-band synchronization in the striato-thalamo-cortical pathway. These cuing effects can resemble those observed via dopaminergic treatments (e.g., levodopa) and deep brain stimulation (DBS) targeting the subthalamic nucleus (STN). Here, we investigated the influence of both levodopa administration and STN DBS on the neural encoding of isochronous auditory sequences in pwPD. A comprehensive analysis of electroencephalography (EEG) data revealed changes in β-band event-locked neural responses, as well as event-related potentials, neural tracking of rhythm (δ-band inter-trial phase coherence), and excitation/inhibition balance (E/I) as a function of these treatments. Furthermore, we characterized the link between changes in E/I and motor symptom severity (UPDRS-III) with levodopa administration. We suggest that characterizing individual responses to specific treatments is a fundamental step in tailoring rehabilitation protocols and optimizing intervention efficacy.

papers.title: Pseudodominant inheritance in paraplegin (SPG7)-associated CPEO-ataxia syndrome.
papers.abstract: SPG7 encodes paraplegin, a mitochondrial AAA-metalloprotease critical for inner mitochondrial membrane protein quality control. Pathogenic variants most commonly cause autosomal recessive hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) but its phenotypic spectrum includes cerebellar ataxia, progressive external ophthalmoplegia, myopathy and parkinsonism.We report a 47 year old man presenting with a progressive external ophthalmoplegia, ptosis, progressive gait disturbance, and spasticity. Ten-year follow-up of this individual showed slowly progressive spastic ataxia with ocular motor involvement and neurogenic bladder. His mother and maternal aunt both had marked spasticity, ataxia, ptosis and external ophthalmoplegia. Genetic testing demonstrated compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in paraplegin in this individual. Genetic testing in his mother and aunt revealed homozygous canonical splice-site variants (c.2182-2 A > G). Cascade testing of his asymptomatic father showed a common pathogenic missense variant p.(Ala510Val) in the same gene.This family demonstrates a pseudodominant inheritance pattern, instead of the expected autosomal recessive trait that applies to paraplegin. We highlight diagnostic pitfalls in relying on family history and assumed inheritance traits. We emphasise the importance of segregation analysis and comprehensive genomic testing. Recognition of pseudodominance inheritance has important implications for genetic counselling, family planning and cascade testing.

papers.title: The Role of Mediterranean, MIND, and Ketogenic Diets in the Management of Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Parkinson's Disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor and nonmotor symptoms due to dopaminergic neuron degeneration. Recently, there has been growing interest in the impact of different dietary patterns on PD management. This review aims to evaluate the potential benefits and risks of the Mediterranean diet, ketogenic diet, and MIND diet in improving PD symptoms and disease progression. RECENT FINDINGS: The Mediterranean diet, rich in antioxidants and anti-inflammatory components, may help alleviate PD symptoms and slow disease progression. The ketogenic diet has shown promise in improving motor symptoms through the neuroprotective effects of ketone bodies. The MIND diet, known for its cognitive health benefits, may help mitigate cognitive decline in PD patients. However, studies directly assessing the efficacy of these diets in PD are still limited. A balanced diet plays a crucial role in managing PD symptoms and enhancing the quality of life. While current evidence suggests potential benefits of specific dietary patterns, further large-scale and long-term studies are necessary to determine their direct effects on PD progression and symptom management.

papers.title: Gut microbiota-derived TNF-α triggers dopaminergic neuron ferroptosis via TNFR1-NF-κB-ATF4 axis in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) pathogenesis remains incompletely understood, with the causal link between gut microbiota dysbiosis and central neurodegeneration unclarified. This study aimed to unravel this complex interplay by integrating Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis, animal models, cellular experiments, and transcriptomic profiling. MR analysis identified Clostridium sensu stricto 1 and Candidatus Soleaferrea as novel genetic risk factors for PD, providing causal evidence for gut microbiota-driven PD pathogenesis. Using a chronic MPTP-induced PD mouse model, we confirmed that gut microbiota dysbiosis is accompanied by elevated tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) in the intestine, plasma, and midbrain, along with dopaminergic neuron loss and motor deficits. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from healthy mice reversed these phenotypes, restoring gut homeostasis, reducing TNF-α levels, and preserving dopaminergic neurons. Transcriptomic analysis of mouse midbrain and human PD substantia nigra (GEO datasets) revealed ferroptosis as a key enriched pathway, with activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) significantly upregulated in both PD models and patients. Mechanistically, TNF-α induced ATF4 overexpression in a concentration- and time-dependent manner, triggering dopaminergic neuron ferroptosis. This effect was mediated by TNF-α binding to TNFR1 (not TNFR2), activating the NF-κB pathway, and subsequently upregulating ATF4. Knockdown of ATF4 or inhibition of NF-κB reversed TNF-α-induced ferroptosis, as evidenced by restored glutathione (GSH) levels, reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) accumulation, and improved cell viability. Our findings establish a novel gut-brain axis-mediated pathogenic pathway: gut microbiota dysbiosis drives TNF-α-TNFR1-NF-κB-ATF4 signaling, leading to dopaminergic neuron ferroptosis and PD progression. This study bridges the gap between peripheral microbial dysbiosis and central neurode

papers.title: Fluctuations correlates in advanced dementia with Lewy bodies: A longitudinal study.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cognitive fluctuations are a core feature of dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). Research focuses largely on early stages. We investigated fluctuation frequency and correlates in advanced DLB. METHODS: The Mayo Fluctuations Scale and Clinician Assessment of Fluctuations measured fluctuations. Analyses assessed frequency, scale correlations, and experiences correlating with baseline and longitudinal fluctuations. RESULTS: Fluctuations occurred in > 70% of the cohort across visits. Fluctuation scales correlated very weakly. Baseline fluctuations correlated with female sex, symptom burden, cognitive severity, neuropsychiatric symptom burden, hallucinations, sleepiness/alertness, parkinsonism, autonomic symptom burden, and orthostatic hypotension. Additional variables correlated with single scales. Fluctuations weakly correlated with participant quality of life and caregiver experiences. Longitudinal fluctuations correlated with other DLB features, comorbidities, and medication burden. DISCUSSION: Fluctuations are common in advanced DLB and correlate with other symptoms. Fluctuation measurement requires further conceptual and psychometric work for best approaches, including for screening and longitudinal assessments and treatment trials. STUDY REGISTRATION: NCT04829656.

papers.title: AI-Driven Discovery and Delivery Systems for Anti-Parkinsonian Agents.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease is the second most widely diagnosed neurodegenerative disorder in the world, affecting more than 10 million people, with current drug therapies for treatment providing limited symptomatic relief and no effect on stopping disease progression. The integration of AI and Pharmaceutical Sciences has led to a change in the approach to discovering and developing new anti-Parkinsonian drugs. This review presents a comprehensive overview of the many applications of Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Generative AI to the PD drug development process.We have critically examined AI-guided target identification, including disruption of α-synuclein (SNCA) fibrils, inhibition of Leucine Rich Repeat Kinase 2 (LRRK2), modulation of GBA1/Glucocerebrosidase and restoration of mitochondrial functions via PINK1/Parkin along with the application of Transformer-based models such as AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold to elucidate the structures of Pathological proteins and create the basis for conducting AI-accelerated Virtual Screening studies, yielding exciting lead compounds.Although tremendous advancements have been made, many obstacles need to be overcome, such as obtaining rare disease data, improving the interpretability of the data used in AI models, developing appropriate regulatory pathways, and bridging the gap between pre-clinical and clinical data.
